tb21_profile.skill: Speed up a numerical simulation by ~1.7x purely through solver/integrator/discretisation settings, keeping the final state within 1e-5 of the reference — measure, change one knob, re-measure
tb21_profile.domain: MuJoCo physics engine and MJCF XML configuration; numerical integrators, solver iterations/tolerances, timestep and contact settings; scientific computing
tb21_profile.task_form: optimise-for-a-budget: hit a runtime target under a hard numerical-equivalence constraint, by editing configuration rather than rewriting code

searches: tools.py search all "physics simulation|rigid body|collision detection" -n 30
tools.py search all "speedup of at least|speedup >=|faster than the (baseline|reference)|runtime .{0,20}reduc"
tools.py search all "speedup of at least|speedup >=|speedup of|must achieve a .{0,20}speedup|faster than the (baseline|reference)" -n 42
tools.py show task_000269_3b0056a6 task_000140_40bb239d task_000048_b0bd6829 task_000157_45d18f63
tools.py search tw "benchmark|wall-clock|execution time|performance test|speedup|tune the|parameter sweep" -n 30

TMax-15K.reason: Swap the ODE integrator so a stiff simulation finishes fast, with an assertion that the result stays within 1e-5 of the exact value — the same trade.
Fix a diverging integrator and make it >=2x faster than an oracle while matching its output to 1e-6; integrator choice and step control.
Reach a 50x speedup on a numerical computation while keeping the answer within 1e-5 of the naive method — speed under an accuracy constraint.
Profile a mechanical simulation, replace the solver, and hit 5x while the output stays mathematically equivalent (MSE < 1e-4).
Adaptive step-size logic is inverted, so steps grow when local error grows; reasoning about step size versus error is the core of this tuning.
Run a mesh-refinement convergence study and tabulate error versus discretisation — how coarse you can go before the tolerance breaks.
Discretisation error fails to shrink at the expected O(h^2) rate; understanding a scheme's accuracy order is what makes a bigger timestep safe.
Make the pipeline significantly faster while the output must match a reference array to MSE < 1e-8; same two-sided constraint.
An adaptive Runge-Kutta change broke a reaction-diffusion simulator; diagnosing integrator settings inside a simulation package.
Partition a CFD mesh 3x faster while producing byte-identical HDF5 output; optimisation constrained by exact-output equality.

Graph metadata leaks into scheduler optimisation routines; optimisation passes that must not change the computed result.
A piecewise loss misbehaves for very small beta; reasoning about a numerical parameter's regime, as with tiny timesteps.

Rounding of fractional indices when slicing a discretised array; off-by-a-fraction discretisation bugs.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Making relative and absolute solver tolerances settable — literally the knob that trades simulation speed against accuracy here.
Discretisation point counts and solver selection for a physics simulation; coarser mesh versus accuracy is the same decision.
A nonlinear solver's convergence criterion only takes effect one iteration late, so it does extra work; solver iteration accounting.
Simulation termination events fire inconsistently between solvers; the same solution must come out whichever solver runs.
A simulation misbehaves under a particular configuration; debugging a physics model's run settings.
Nonlinear solver configuration on a coupled model; wiring solver options through a simulation framework.
Parameter-set and solver interaction in a battery simulation; model parameters versus solver behaviour.
Decomposing a system into strongly connected blocks so the solver does far less work for the same answer.
Nonlinear solver setup for a coupled circuit model that must converge; solver choice on a stiff coupled system.
Tridiagonal (Thomas algorithm) solver and its differentiation support; numerical solver internals in an array framework.

final_top10.reason: Change the integrator so a stiff simulation runs fast while asserting the answer stays within 1e-5 — the identical speed/accuracy trade.
Fix divergence and beat an oracle by 2x while matching its output to 1e-6; step control and integrator choice under a tolerance.
Hit a hard speedup target while the numerical result must stay within 1e-5 of the reference implementation.
Profile a simulation to find the bottleneck, replace the solver, and keep the output mathematically equivalent while hitting 5x.
Inverted adaptive step-size logic; step size versus local error is exactly the reasoning a bigger MuJoCo timestep needs.
Exposes relative and absolute solver tolerances on a physics simulation — the same knob, in another simulator.
Mesh-refinement convergence study: measure error as discretisation coarsens, which is how you pick the cheapest safe setting.
Discretisation point counts plus solver choice for a simulation; cost is set by resolution and solver, as in MJCF.
Error must fall at the scheme's expected order as the grid refines; knowing that order is what licenses a coarser setting.
Significant speedup required while the output must match a reference to MSE < 1e-8; both constraints binding at once.

notes: Only one task in the whole pool mentions MuJoCo at all (tw_471679, which just installs it), so domain-5 matches essentially do not exist and I ranked on skill: speed up a numerical simulation without moving its output. TMax is by far the strongest corpus here — it has a large, genuinely relevant cluster of 'X-times speedup with output within tolerance' tasks plus a separate cluster on integrator choice, step-size adaptation and convergence order, which is the actual physics-solver knowledge this task needs; task_000269_3b0056a6 is close to a duplicate of the TB task in a different simulator. SWE-Rebench contributes real value through pybamm/openmdao/pyomo (solver tolerances, discretisation, convergence criteria) even though the task_form never matches. SWE-Smith is the weak corpus: it contains no numerical-simulation repos, so its entries top out around overall 2 and ranks 9-10 there are filler. One caution for merge: the 'must achieve a speedup of Nx' family in TMax is large (40+ tasks) and mostly about rewriting slow code in a faster language, which is NOT this task — this task forbids changing the physics and only allows config. I kept the ones where a numerical tolerance also binds and dropped the pure rewrite-it-in-Rust ones.
